cards.text: Acts 4:25 says David spoke the words of this psalm. He opens with a big question about the whole world: 'Why do the nations rage and the peoples plot in vain?' Raging AND plotting, friend? That's a FULL schedule.

cards.question: True or false: When David says the peoples plot in vain, he means their plan is going to work.

cards.text: Then the kings of the earth take their stand, and the rulers gather together. Biggest meeting in the world, and NOBODY brought cookies.

cards.question: The kings of the earth and the rulers take their stand together. Who are they standing against?

answers.text: The LORD and His Anointed One
Moses and the elders of Israel
Elijah and the prophets of God

cards.text: Here's their big plan: 'Let us break Their chains and cast away Their cords.' It's a group chat full of coworkers planning to tell off the boss, and EVERYBODY is typing in all caps.

cards.question: The kings want to break the chains and cast away the cords of the LORD and His Anointed One. What are they really saying?

answers.text: We won't be ruled by Them
We want Them to lead us
We need Them to protect us

cards.question: The kings are plotting down on earth. Meanwhile, the One enthroned in heaven ___.

cards.text: He laughs, and the Lord taunts them. Their plan is about as believable as me telling the whole bakery I'm only eating ONE cookie today.

cards.question: True or false: After laughing at the plotting kings, God just lets their plot slide.

cards.text: Then He rebukes them in His anger, and terrifies them in His fury. And what He says next shuts that whole meeting down.

cards.question: The kings are plotting against the LORD and His Anointed One. What does God announce He has already done?

answers.text: Sent a flood over the earth

cards.text: 'I have installed My King on Zion, upon My holy mountain.' The kings are still plotting to break free, and the King is already in place.
Now the King Himself speaks up, ready to proclaim the decree the LORD spoke to Him. The kings brought a group chat. He brought a DECREE.

cards.question: In the decree, the LORD calls the King His ___ and says that today He has become His Father.

cards.text: Of every name I've ever been called, Papa is the best one, so a Father talking to His Son like that gets me EVERY time. I'm not crying, friend, the oven's just running hot.

cards.question: All the Son has to do is ask. True or false: If He asks, the LORD will make the nations the Son's inheritance and the ends of the earth His possession.
The LORD tells the Son He will break the nations with an iron scepter. What will the Son shatter them like?

cards.text: Then the psalm turns straight to the rulers: 'Therefore be wise, O kings; be admonished, O judges of the earth.' And just like that, the group chat goes REAL quiet.

cards.question: The kings of the earth are told to be wise. What does being wise look like for them?

cards.text: Right alongside that, they're told to rejoice with trembling. That's me opening the oven on a brand-new recipe, friend, excited and SHAKING.
Then the kings get one more instruction: 'Kiss the Son.' Friend, these guys showed up to break chains, and that meeting did NOT end the way they drew it up.

cards.question: The kings are told to kiss the Son, or He may be angry and they could perish in their ___.
After all that warning to the kings, the psalm ends with good news. Who does it call blessed?

answers.text: All who take refuge in Him
All who rule over the earth

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: the Acts 4:25 line, the line with the quote of Psalm 2:1, 'Raging AND plotting, friend?' and 'That's a FULL schedule.'

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The card opens with 'Then the kings of the earth take their stand', which puts verse 2 after verse 1 in time. The text gives no sequence. Verse 2 describes the same raging and plotting that verse 1 asks about.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The storyteller line 'And what He says next shuts that whole meeting down' states an outcome the text never gives. Psalm 2:5-6 doesn't say the kings' gathering ends or stops.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can add a storyteller's line to carry the moment, like "But the Lord isn't finished with him," as long as it adds no facts.

findings.problem: The joke 'The kings brought a group chat. He brought a DECREE.' blends the group chat comparison into the Bible setting, as if the kings literally had a group chat.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: This story card only gives Papa Dorin's reaction to verse 7, which card 2 already covered. It tells no new part of the passage and doesn't move the baker forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: Asking what the Son will shatter the nations like (pottery, dry reeds or cedar trees) asks the baker to guess a detail of the line's wording. Nothing earlier lets them reason it out. This matches the Psalm 23 'anoint David's head with' bad example. There is also no story card setting up verses 8-9.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: 'And just like that, the group chat goes REAL quiet' blends the group chat comparison into the Bible setting. It also gives the kings a reaction the text never describes.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.
